messages:
ajay: heads up — since the 03:00 deploy i'm seeing repeated gRPC streams drop between gpu-pool-a pods. model shards keep restarting streams mid-token, clients see 5xx and stalls.
ops-oncall: alert triggered: grpc_stream_error_rate > 4% on gpu-pool-a (03:08) — rolling 5m. Affected nodes: n-gpu-12..n-gpu-17.
kevin: can you grab a tcpdump from one of the src pods and from the node egress? suspect MTU/encap.
maria: attached quick pcap snippet — lots of ICMP "fragmentation needed" and then retransmits. also seeing series of small fragments not reassembled:
```
16:42:12.345678 IP 10.32.4.12 > 10.32.6.21: UDP, length 1472
16:42:12.345680 IP (frag 8192|8193) ...
ICMP frag needed, df set, mtu 1400
```
ajay: interesting — gRPC uses HTTP/2 over TCP, why UDP frags? our overlay uses geneve/udp encapsulation for east-west, so underlying packets get bigger.
sara: quick checklist — check host MTU, overlay MTU, and NIC offloads (GSO/GRO). also verify SR-IOV VF MTU if present.
kevin: run on node: `ip link show` and `ip -d link show geneve0` helped. on n-gpu-14: host mtu 1500, geneve0 mtu 1450, vf0 mtu 1500 -> mismatch creeping in after a recent NIC firmware reflash.
shawn: firmware changed default L3 cap; VF/host vs encapsulation didn't recompute effective mtu. that can make encapsulated packets exceed path MTU and DF triggers.
maria: here's a quick mitigation I tried — enabled TCP MSS clamping in iptables on the nodes hosting the pods: `iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` — reduced downstream stalls in my test.
kevin: good short-term. long-term we should set overlay MTU to account for encap overhead (geneve/geneve_options) and ensure CNI config matches. calico/vxlan typically needs mtu ~1450 if nic 1500 and encap is 50 bytes.
sara: also check NIC offloads — if GSO is on but kernel cannot offload for encapsulated packets, we get giant frames that get chopped by intermediate switch/driver. run `ethtool -k eth0` and look for gso/gro/tx-udp_tnl-segmentation.
ajay: RDMA note — some of the GPU hosts have HCA and GPUDirect with RoCE enabled. RDMA paths are fine, but model shard replication falls back to TCP over geneve for control streams — that's what's stalling.
devops-bot: deploys: 03:02 rolling FW update applied to n-gpu-* (reason: security). Firmware rollback scheduled? :information_source:
shawn: suggest plan: 1) set node iptables MSS clamp as stopgap, 2) adjust CNI MTU to 1400 across gpu pools, 3) coordinate NIC firmware rollforward with vendor to keep VF MTUs consistent, 4) enable net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on affected nodes to recover quicker.
kevin: commands: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1`, `kubectl -n kube-system get ds calico-node -o yaml | grep mtu` to patch, or `kubectl patch ds/calico-node --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"calico-node","env":[{"name":"FELIX_DEFAULTENDPOINTMTU","value":"1400"}]}]}}}}'`.
maria: tested `ip link set geneve0 mtu 1400` on a node and restarted a failing pod: stream resumed, no more mid-token resets. ops side wants a safer rollout.
ops-oncall: scheduling <maintenance> 2h window to change CNI MTU on gpu pools and cordon+drain nodes in small batches. Please add runbook steps.
ajay: runbook note — remember to update HAProxy/ingress config for backend keepalive and max_frame_size if we change MSS. also add a smoke test hitting a long-polling gRPC endpoint to verify no mid-stream resets.
sara: adding to runbook: checks for `ss -s` retransmit counters, `dmesg` for NIC driver FRAG or PMTU logs, and sample tcpdump to confirm no ICMP frag-needed after change.
kevin: after we patch, follow-up: verify SR-IOV VF MTU alignment and re-run long-tail perf tests (p99 latency of gRPC streams).
ajay: thanks — taking lead on the rollout plan. ping me for node list. :thumbsup:
